heroByline: Produced By Ant Open Source & InclusionAI · September 2026
heroLede: This report studies more than 100 open-source projects in the Agentic AI ecosystem and compares them with established software repositories. It looks at how agents are entering everyday development work, and what open infrastructure must manage when their actions reach production. Final abstract to be confirmed.
voicesIntro: Opening notes on the Agentic AI ecosystem.
zhengyuQuote: Quote to be confirmed before publication.
xuQuote: Quote to be confirmed before publication.
mergeGateTitle: Agents are working inside the repository
mergeGateBody: Agents read contribution rules, edit files, run tests and respond to review. That puts them inside the ordinary Issue and pull-request loop. The question is whether they shorten the path to a useful change or mainly increase the volume that maintainers have to judge.
executionGateTitle: Agents bring code to the runtime
executionGateBody: An agent may write code after a task has started, open a browser, call internal services and keep state across several short-lived environments. Infrastructure has to isolate work it has never seen before, limit the authority of each task and preserve enough evidence to explain what changed after the process is gone.
landscapeOverviewTitle: Agent applications lead the activity. Runtime is where the landscape is filling in.
landscapeOverviewBody: The current landscapes contain 84 Agent Infra and 59 Model Infra projects. Applications hold 55% of Agent Infra's July OpenRank, while Runtime accounts for 13 of the 23 Agent Infra selections outside the May tracking pool. Model Infra remains an older, Python-led systems base, with Serving holding 44% of its July OpenRank. The map shows both where activity sits and where production responsibilities are accumulating.
landscapeTitle: Applications hold the activity. Runtime holds more of the new selections.
agentChartTitle: Attention is still concentrated at the application layer
modelChartTitle: Serving still carries the systems weight
ageFinding: The agent layer is being invented quickly. Most of the infrastructure underneath it predates the current wave and is being asked to carry a different task shape.
languageTitle: Agent products lean TypeScript. Model infrastructure still speaks Python.
languageBody: TypeScript leads Agent Infra with 33 of 84 repositories; Python leads Model Infra with 33 of 59. This is GitHub’s primary language per repository, not a share of source lines; Other includes Rust, Java, Shell and smaller groups.
runtimePathTitle: Runtime projects are clustering along the path an agent takes through a task.
runtimePathBody: The map is filling in around context, interfaces, tool execution, isolation and evidence. These categories connect the project landscape to the task now reaching Kubernetes, OpenInfra, workload identity and telemetry systems.
growthSummary: Recent OpenRank gains appear around tool use, context and inference efficiency. They show community activity, not production adoption.
outsideGithubTitle: The same workload is visible beyond repository activity.
outsideGithubBody: Nine of OpenRouter’s current global Top 20 apps map directly to projects in Agent Infra. OpenRouter is an opt-in ranking checked on 29 August 2026; ZenMux is a separate snapshot for 1–30 June. Their token totals stay separate, and neither source measures unique users or deployments.
collaborationTitle: Repositories are changing in two places: their instructions and their public threads.
collaborationLede: We first inspect the files that tell coding agents how to work inside each repository. Later, as a separate analysis, we examine 2,000 sampled Issues and pull requests to see which Agent actions are visible in public collaboration.
collaborationProfileBody: We froze the 100 highest-July-OpenRank repositories in the 277-project tracking pool, then reviewed every project for LLM dependence and technical role. Backlog counts cover items opened since 1 January 2026; actor groups can overlap and include public automation accounts.
collaborationAdoptionTitle: 92 of the Top 100 repositories have set up files or folders for coding agents.
collaborationAdoptionBody: The scan includes instruction files such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, as well as tool folders such as .claude, .cursor, .codex and .gemini. We treat either as repository-level adoption of a coding-agent workflow.
collaborationTasksTitle: Most Agent activity we can see is review, triage and replies.
collaborationTasksBody: In the 2,000 Issues and pull requests we reviewed, named coding and review agents appeared far more often in comments and reviews than in thread openings or commits. These are public Agent-attributed events, not labour shares; a thread can contain several tasks, and Bot/App and Agent categories can overlap.
collaborationEntryTitle: Agents gather in the middle of the thread.
collaborationEntryBody: After adjusting for repository size, Agents open less than one percent of Issues and pull requests, yet appear in about a third of pull-request review. Open uses all 2,000 sampled threads, Review uses sampled PRs, and Gate uses resolved threads with a visible final actor; rows can overlap when an App mediates a User action.
collaborationIterationTitle: Review still produces a real revision loop.
collaborationIterationBody: A visible review appears in six out of ten sampled PRs. Among the 63 PRs with a visible change request, a later commit appears in 80.5% of Agent-attributed cases and 71.5% of GitHub User cases. The difference is descriptive; it does not estimate efficiency or prove that review caused the change.
collaborationLineageTitle: Most of the first Agent patch stayed. The route to merge still varied.
collaborationLineageBody: We replayed every merged PR in the probability sample where a verified Coding Agent touched the code. Nine of ten cases had a line-traceable patch, and 62.4% of its first text remained. Exact survival is not semantic authorship, and GitHub User accounts may use private AI. Mooncake #2686 stays outside the denominator because its Agent-attributed commit is a two-parent merge.
collaborationGovernanceTitle: Open contribution remains the norm. More projects ask contributors to align before coding.
collaborationGovernanceBody: All 100 repositories enable Pull Requests, but creation access is not identical. Ninety-eight allow anyone to create one; Codex and Claude Code restrict creation to collaborators. Twelve more use an Issue-first or scoped pre-approval rule. DeepSeek Harness remains a useful outlier outside the denominator: public code, closed core contribution and a plugin-led extension path.
collaborationBurdenTitle: Agents expanded throughput. Human attention did not scale with it.
collaborationBurdenBody: Across ten matched repositories, incoming Issues and pull requests grew 165% while seven-day maintainer response fell from 42.9% to 20.0%. Thirty-day Issue closure and PR merge also fell. Agent-visible threads show denser iteration, but no clear outcome advantage.
collaborationScarcityTitle: The scarce contribution is a decision that survives review.
collaborationScarcityBody: External accounts create most pull requests in the weighted sample. Their resolved PRs carry GitHub's merged flag far less often than maintainer or member submissions. Code is abundant at the entrance; review, task selection and a defensible gate remain scarce.
caseTitle: The contribution surface sits outside the core repository
caseQuote: “You may consider this repository an idea, an official showcase, and a source of inspiration, but not a mandate from us.”
caseBody: The project treats its official code as a reference point and third-party plugins as the place where the ecosystem can branch out. That arrangement leaves practical governance work around interface stability, discovery and what happens when a plugin becomes unsafe or abandoned.
governanceInterface: Interface stability needs a visible owner.
governanceDiscovery: Plugin discovery needs verification and provenance.
governanceRevocation: Unsafe or abandoned capabilities need a revocation path.
studyNote: The thread estimates use a frozen Top 100, a 2,000-thread repository-stratified probability sample and an equal-repository view. GitHub User means account type, not human-written code. GitHub merged flag is not a universal accepted-contribution label.
infrastructureTitle: Agent execution is variable, stateful and capable of side effects.
infrastructureLede: A task can generate code after it starts, fan out across model and tool calls, pause, retry and leave a change behind. Public token totals do not tell us task-level QPS. The harder infrastructure problem is keeping isolation, authority, budget, state and evidence attached to the same task while its processes come and go.
infrastructureProjectTitle: Open projects cover much of the path. The gaps sit between them.
infrastructureProjectBody: Some projects were built for agents. Others bring mature isolation, identity, scheduling and tracing into the task. The remaining work is task-wide: budgets, cancellation, safe recovery and evidence still stop at component boundaries.
closingQuestion: Can an agent run code, use authority and leave enough evidence for someone else to understand what happened?
closingNote: This is where agentic AI meets cloud native, PyTorch and OpenInfra. The established stack remains useful. Its control model has to account for code and environments that appear during the task.
